features.purpose: Drive registered Three.js clips from semantic states on deterministic client ticks, including crossfades and one-shot completion events.
features.ownership: The Animation runtime owns its mixer/actions and borrows the caller's Object3D and AnimationClip objects; the Feature owns the injected runtime after successful setup.

clips.bounds: At least one clip; IDs are trimmed and at most 128 characters.

authority.intent: Animation is non-authoritative presentation and cannot change trusted gameplay state.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates animation-update; activation failure leaves the runtime caller-owned for explicit cleanup.
lifecycle.dispose: Shutdown or rollback removes completion listeners, stops and uncaches every action/root, clears retained references, and is idempotent.
borrowedResources: The Object3D and clip objects remain caller-owned; their geometry, material, texture, and asset disposal belongs to the Asset Manager or caller.

limitations: Animation is client-only and advances at the fixed simulation rate.
Root motion is deliberately ignored; authoritative motion must come from gameplay/Character Controller state.
State transitions use one active action and do not provide blend trees, masks, or inverse kinematics.

features.purpose: Load glTF, texture, and audio assets from manifests with groups, cache deduplication, progress, structured failures, and deterministic disposal.
features.ownership: The manager owns successful backend load results until disposal; the backend owns its loader internals, while manifest values and progress callbacks remain caller-owned.

manifest.bounds: Unique IDs; gltf, texture, or audio kind; bounded sources; unique groups.

backend.bounds: Must load, disposeAsset, and dispose; audio requires a caller-supplied loadAudio adapter.

authority.intent: Asset loading is a local client capability and conveys no gameplay authority.

lifecycle.setup: The manager is created before boot; Feature setup establishes ownership and has no scheduled system.
lifecycle.dispose: Shutdown/rollback releases cached assets once, fences in-flight results so late values are immediately disposed, clears listeners/references, then disposes the backend.
borrowedResources: Manifest records and progress callback functions remain caller-owned; the manager stores validated immutable copies of manifest records.

limitations: The default Three backend needs browser loader facilities and a loadAudio adapter for audio decoding.
Cache entries remain resident until manager disposal; per-asset reference counting and eviction are not implemented.
Cancellation cannot abort vendor network I/O, but late results are fenced and disposed.

features.purpose: Provide sound effects, looping music, buses, mute/volume controls, optional positional playback, browser unlock, and a silent fallback.
features.ownership: The Audio runtime owns registered buffer references, live voices, and its injected driver after successful Feature setup.

driver.bounds: Use createWebAudioDriver with a valid Web Audio context for playback.

clips.bounds: Unique trimmed IDs at most 128 characters.

authority.intent: Audio is non-authoritative presentation and cannot affect simulation state.

lifecycle.setup: The Audio runtime is constructed before boot; Feature setup establishes ownership and has no scheduled system. Call unlock from a browser user gesture.
lifecycle.dispose: Shutdown/rollback stops every voice, disconnects owned Web Audio nodes, clears clip references, and disposes the driver exactly once.
borrowedResources: The browser AudioContext is caller-owned and is not closed by createWebAudioDriver; the caller decides when to close it.

limitations: The built-in buses apply scalar gain to voices and do not expose arbitrary Web Audio graphs.
Positional playback configures a PannerNode position but leaves listener orientation and distance-model policy to the host.
The silent fallback validates calls but intentionally produces no sound.

features.purpose: Apply deterministic walk/run, gravity, grounded jump, platform velocity, and external impulses above the public collision adapter.
features.ownership: The controller owns the injected ClientCollisionAdapter; the Feature owns the controller after successful setup while input and publish callbacks remain caller-owned.

collision.bounds: Must provide move and dispose; use createRapierCollisionAdapter for the bundled implementation.

locomotion.bounds: Positive finite walk/run/gravity/jump/fall values; run speed cannot be below walk speed.

input.bounds: Finite x/z in [-1,1], run/jump booleans, optional finite platform velocity.

authority.intent: The Feature produces local prediction only; an authoritative server must validate movement, grounded/jump state, and impulses independently.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates character-controller-predict; an activation failure leaves the controller caller-owned for explicit cleanup.
lifecycle.dispose: Shutdown/rollback fences ticks and disposes the controller and its collision adapter exactly once.
borrowedResources: readInput and publish callbacks remain caller-owned.

limitations: Slopes, steps, sliding, and contact precision are limited by the selected ClientCollisionAdapter.
Moving platforms are supplied as a caller-computed velocity hook; platform ownership/contact discovery is outside this Feature.
This is prediction, not authority or network reconciliation; install it instead of the lower-level collision Feature when it owns the same adapter.

features.purpose: Compute and publish one collision move per client prediction tick.
features.ownership: The Feature owns the injected ClientCollisionAdapter after successful setup; the caller owns the position, translation, and publish callbacks.

adapter.bounds: Must provide move and dispose functions.

readStartPosition.type: function returning exactly finite x, y, and z numbers
readStartPosition.bounds: All three components must be finite.

readDesiredTranslation.type: function returning exactly finite x, y, and z numbers
readDesiredTranslation.bounds: All three components must be finite.

authority.intent: Client prediction is non-authoritative; a server must independently validate authoritative movement.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates collision-shared-predict through the Feature-scoped lifecycle ledger. Failed activation resets the active fence and rethrows; the caller must dispose the retained adapter if this Feature's own activation fails.
lifecycle.dispose: After successful setup, disposal disables the system and disposes the owned adapter exactly once. A disposed descriptor cannot be set up or moved again.
borrowedResources: The readStartPosition, readDesiredTranslation, and publish callbacks remain caller-owned.

limitations: The bundled adapter is a bounded local predictor with zero gravity, one kinematic capsule-like controller, sliding enabled, autostep and snap-to-ground disabled, and static boxes only.
It provides no dynamic rigid bodies, broad gameplay physics, reconciliation, or authority.
A failed adapter outcome becomes a system error.
Runtime configuration accepts only an empty object.

features.purpose: Accept a semantic Interaction intent, validate it on the authoritative server, toggle one configured target, replicate that state, and present it on clients.

authority.intent: The client queues only a targetEntityId; it cannot directly change target state.
validation: The command must pass protocol schema, connection phase, sequence, tick-window, queue, and owned-actor validation.
The targetEntityId must equal the configured targetEntityId.
The actor position must be within the configured inclusive Euclidean range of the target position.
Only a previously accepted Interaction is applied, and each application toggles authoritative active state once.
The server replicates the resulting interactable snapshot state to clients.

lifecycle.setup: Each descriptor validates its exact configuration before setup. The server acquires its adapter state before activation; the client acquires its control state before activating its presentation system. A setup failure rolls back acquired state.
lifecycle.dispose: Each Feature releases only records it acquired through its lifecycle ledger. Shutdown and rollback release remaining owned records in reverse acquisition order, and repeated shutdown is safe.
borrowedResources: The server borrows host.authoritative-interaction and never disposes, closes, transfers, replaces, or republishes it.
The client borrows host.client-replication and never disposes, closes, transfers, replaces, or republishes it.
State or listeners created by the Feature remain Feature-owned and must be released without disposing a borrowed host object.

limitations: Exactly one configured target is supported by the example adapter.
Interaction only toggles a boolean active state; it does not provide inventory, combat, damage, dialogue, navigation, or arbitrary actions.
Feature composition is immutable for a runtime; hot enable, disable, and replacement are unsupported.
The consumer must provide the required server authority and client session Features plus the two host services.
The example uses deterministic finite-distance validation and does not perform line-of-sight or physics-occlusion checks.

features.purpose: Sample and publish one validated semantic movement command per simulation tick.
features.ownership: The input source and publish callback remain caller-owned; the Feature owns no injected disposable resource.

input.bounds: Must provide sample(); sampled commands must have kind move and finite x and z axes within the Shared movement-command bounds.

authority.intent: Published semantic movement is non-authoritative local input and does not grant permission to change server state.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates movement-input-sample through the Feature-scoped lifecycle ledger. Failed activation resets the active fence and rethrows.
lifecycle.dispose: Disposal disables later sampling and publication; it does not dispose the input source or callback.
borrowedResources: The MovementCommandSource and publish callback remain caller-owned.
A caller-owned keyboard adapter retains its two listeners until the caller disposes it.

limitations: The Feature does not retain command history or apply movement.
It does not provide trusted server state, network messaging, input buffering, rebinding, pointer or gamepad input, or authoritative movement decisions.
Runtime configuration accepts only an empty object.

features.purpose: Publish one third-person camera transform per presentation frame.
features.ownership: The target state, configuration input, and callbacks remain caller-owned; the Feature copies and freezes the camera configuration and owns no external resource.

readTarget.type: function returning exactly x, y, and z numbers
readTarget.bounds: All three components must be finite.

bounds.yawRadians: finite number in radians; no default or normalized range

authority.intent: Camera output is non-authoritative presentation data and has no server-visible state.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates third-person-camera-view through the Feature-scoped lifecycle ledger. Failed activation resets the active fence and rethrows.
lifecycle.dispose: Disposal disables later target reads and publication. The Feature owns no camera object or external resource.
borrowedResources: The target state and readTarget and publish callbacks remain caller-owned.

limitations: The Feature does not implement orbit controls, collision avoidance, smoothing, interpolation, zoom limits, occlusion, input binding, or server-visible state.
Presentation frames do not advance simulation.
Runtime configuration accepts only an empty object.

features.purpose: Render the owned renderer scene once per presentation frame.
features.ownership: The Feature owns the injected ClientRendererAdapter after successful setup; attached glTF assets remain borrowed and caller-owned.

renderer.bounds: Must implement avatar asset attachment, avatar and camera updates, resize, render, snapshot, and disposal.

authority.intent: Rendering is non-authoritative presentation work and never changes server or simulation state.

lifecycle.setup: Setup activates three-render-frame through the Feature-scoped lifecycle ledger. If this Feature's own activation fails, the caller must dispose the retained renderer reference.
lifecycle.dispose: After successful setup, disposal disables rendering and disposes the owned renderer exactly once. A disposed descriptor cannot be set up or rendered again.
borrowedResources: Attached glTF assets remain borrowed and must be released by their loader owner.

limitations: The renderer covers only the local MVP scene.
It does not provide post-processing, WebXR, audio, generalized scene management, screenshot-golden guarantees, or server behavior.
Presentation frames do not advance simulation.
Runtime configuration accepts only an empty object.

features.purpose: Present deterministic bounded burst, trail, and floating popup effects before Three.js rendering.
features.ownership: After successful setup the Feature owns the injected VfxRuntime, its Three.js group, pooled objects, geometries, and materials; the parent scene and submitted command values remain caller-owned.

runtime.bounds: Must implement enqueue, present, inspect, and idempotent dispose. createVfxRuntime validates fixed positive capacities and copies every command.

authority.intent: VFX is non-authoritative presentation data and never changes simulation or server state.

lifecycle.setup: Setup acquires vfx-runtime as a renderResources ledger record and activates vfx-present. Failed setup rolls back the owned runtime.
lifecycle.dispose: Disposal is idempotent, removes the owned group, disposes every owned geometry and material, clears queued commands, and releases retained references.
borrowedResources: The parent Three.js Object3D remains caller-owned. Command objects are copied at enqueue and are not retained by reference.

limitations: The runtime provides burst points, line trails, and billboard popup sprites only.
It does not provide audio, post-processing, camera shake, multiplayer replication, dynamic plugin discovery, or text layout.
Presentation requires explicit finite monotonic timestamps and deterministic unsigned 32-bit seeds.
Runtime configuration accepts only an empty object.
